# User guide: Home backup and restore

## In plain words

A home backup is a second, plain copy of a user's home. The home holds the agent sign-ins, memory and chat history of that user. The plugin puts the copy in a folder that you choose, preferably on another drive. If the layers of the home are damaged, or the flash drive fails, you still have the copy. You can run a backup by hand or on a schedule. Each copy is a snapshot. You can restore any snapshot to bring the home back. A restore takes a safety snapshot first, so you can undo it. This page explains each step and each choice.

## Why a backup is not the same as the layers

The plugin already keeps your home on layers. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md). The layers are one copy that the plugin updates all day. They are not a backup, for these reasons:

- They sit in one place. If that drive fails, or a layer is damaged, the home is gone.
- A mistake is copied into them at once. A deleted file stays deleted.
- Only the plugin can read them. You cannot open a layer with a file manager.

A backup is different:

- It is a set of ordinary files. You can open them, copy one file out, or copy the whole folder to another place.
- It lives in a folder that you choose. Choose a drive other than the one that holds your layers when you can.
- It keeps several points in time. You can go back to the state of last Tuesday.

Use both. The layers keep your work safe from a power cut. A backup keeps your home safe from a drive failure and from mistakes.

## Where to find it

Open the **AI CLI Agents** page under Unraid's Settings menu, and open the **Storage** tab. Each home has its own card. At the bottom of the card is the backup strip:

- A line of status text.
- A button. It reads **Set up config backup…** when no folder is chosen. Otherwise it reads **Config backup…**. The backup copies the home folder: the settings, sign-ins and history of the agents. It does not copy the server.

Press the button to open the dialog **Config backup — name** (the name is the Unraid user). Every home has its own settings: its own folder, mode, schedule and snapshots. Two homes can use two folders.

The text under the cards says: "Each home has its own backup: a second, plain copy of the home on a folder you choose, so damage to the Flash layers does not destroy that copy too."

### The status line on the card

| Text | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Config backup is not set up.** | No folder is chosen. |
| **No folder chosen — earlier config backups found in** a path | Snapshots from an earlier setup exist in that path. The dialog offers that folder. |
| **Config not backed up yet · to** a path | A folder is set, but no backup has run. |
| **Backing up config —** a step | A backup is queued, waiting or running. The step changes as the job moves. |
| **Last config backup** time **·** size **(cold)** or **(warm)** | The last backup worked. The line adds the schedule, for example "daily at 02:00". |
| **Last config backup failed:** a reason | The last run did not finish. No snapshot was kept for it. The earlier snapshot is still good. |

A warm backup can add "· N files changed during the backup". This is not an error. See "Cold and warm" below.

## How to use it

### Set up a backup

1. Open the **Storage** tab.
2. Press **Set up config backup…** on the card of the home.
3. Press **Choose folder…** under **Destination folder**. Expect: the plugin's folder browser opens.
4. Go to the folder that should hold the snapshots. The browser has a **New folder** button. It makes a folder for you. Press **Select**.
5. Read the result line under the folder. Expect: a check mark, the real path, the file system, and the free space, for example "/mnt/cache/backups (xfs) — 812.4 GB free". If you see a cross and a reason, choose another folder.
6. Choose the other settings in the dialog. Each setting saves the moment you change it.
7. Press **Back up now** for the first backup.

The dialog shows "Saving…" beside a field, then "Saved". If the plugin refuses a value, the field shows "Not saved:" with the reason and goes back to the last saved value. The dialog never shows a value that is not saved.

The dialog checks the saved folder each time it opens. This catches a drive that someone unplugged.

> [!NOTE]
> The result line under the folder is the check. There is no separate **Check** button. The plugin checks a folder when you select it and when the dialog opens.

### Choose a destination folder

A good folder is on a pool, on an Unassigned Devices drive, or on an array disk. Rules:

- A folder under `/mnt/user` is not saved as you typed it. A home has many thousands of small files, and copying them through Unraid's shared-folder layer can freeze the server. The plugin saves the real pool or disk path of the share instead. If it cannot find one, it refuses the folder and gives the reason.
- A folder in RAM or on the Unraid flash drive is refused. This includes `/tmp`, `/root`, `/dev/shm`, `/boot`, and a path that reaches them with `..`. A backup there is lost at reboot, or the flash drive cannot hold the "latest" link. Choose a folder on a pool, a disk or an Unassigned Devices drive.
- The folder must be writable.
- The folder must not be inside a home or inside the plugin's own storage folder.
- The folder needs free space of at least 1.5 times the size of the home.

If a home has no folder but earlier snapshots exist, the dialog says "Your earlier backups are in" a path, with the button **Use this folder**. The plugin never chooses that folder by itself.

On a phone the dialog fits the screen. Every button is at least 44 pixels tall and the fields use a size that stops the browser from zooming in.

### Cold and warm

| Mode | What the plugin does | Result | Cost |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Cold** (default) — "closes the sessions first, most consistent" | Closes every open workspace of the user, saves the home, copies it, checks the copy, and reopens the workspaces. | The most consistent copy. The agents' databases are safe to copy only when the agent is not running. | The workspaces close for the time of the copy. |
| **Warm** — "sessions keep running, best effort" | Copies the home while the workspaces run. | A copy without a pause. Files can change during the copy. | The copy is best effort. The snapshot carries the label "warm". |

In a warm backup, the plugin counts the files that changed while it copied. It shows "N files changed during the backup". A database that changed during the copy is copied again with the safe-copy feature of SQLite (the database engine that agents use). The snapshot is complete. The backup fails only when a file differs from the home for a reason other than a change during the backup.

Use warm only when a short pause is not acceptable. Cold is the better choice for a nightly schedule at 02:00.

### Continue on relaunch

A cold backup closes the workspaces and reopens them. The plugin looks at each workspace just before it closes and notes whether the agent was working or was waiting at its prompt. After the reopen, the plugin sends one Continue message to each agent that was working. An agent that was waiting gets nothing.

The checkbox **Tell an agent to continue if it was working when the backup started** controls this. It is ticked by default. Untick it when you want no message after the reopen. The agents then use no tokens (the paid units of an AI model) until you tell them to go on. The setting does not apply to a warm backup, because nothing closes.

### Schedule

| Field | Choices | Default |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Schedule** | **Off**, **Daily**, **Weekly** | **Off** |
| Day (weekly only) | Sunday to Saturday | Sunday |
| Time (daily and weekly) | A time of day | 02:00 |

The plugin owns one scheduled job for each home that has a schedule. A home with **Off** has none. The schedule runs the same backup as **Back up now**, with the mode you chose. If a scheduled backup fails, the plugin writes the reason to the log.

The Health check for backups warns when the last snapshot of a home is older than twice the schedule interval. Without a schedule, it warns after 7 days. The text reads, for example, "root's last home backup was 3.2 day(s) ago". See [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md).

### Retention

**Keep** is the number of snapshots the plugin holds for the home. The range is 1 to 50. The default is 5. After each good backup, the plugin removes the oldest snapshots beyond that number. It never removes the newest snapshot.

A snapshot you delete by hand lowers the count. The next backup does not refill the gap.

### Back up now

1. Press **Back up now** in the footer of the dialog. The button is dimmed while no folder is set, and while a backup or restore of this home runs. Hover to read why.
2. Read the confirmation **Back up name’s home now?** It says whether sessions close (cold) or keep running (warm).
3. Press **Back up now**. Expect: "Queued — Watch the activity tray for progress."

The Activity tray shows the steps: pre-flight (the checks), closing, baking (saving the home to a layer), copying, verifying and relaunching. The card shows "Backing up —" and the current step. A backup waits if a save or merge of the same home is already running. The tray then shows "waiting". A backup does not start while a merge runs; the page tells you so.

### Exclude files

Open **Advanced: excluded files** in the dialog. One pattern per line. The plugin skips these files in the copy. The default list holds caches that a program can download again:

- `.claude/plugins/**`
- `**/node_modules/**`
- `.grok/marketplace-cache/**`
- `.gemini/antigravity-cli/**`
- `.cache/**`
- `.claude/image-cache/**`
- `**/*.tmp`

The plugin saves the list when you leave the field. Patterns may hold letters, digits, spaces and the characters `_ . / * -`. The secrets of the agents are included in a backup on purpose, because a restore must bring back the sign-ins.

## What a snapshot holds

A snapshot holds the files of the home as the agents see them. It is the content of the home, not the layers. The plugin never copies layer files into a backup.

In your chosen folder, the plugin makes this structure:

- a folder `aicli-home-backup`;
- inside it, one folder for each user;
- inside that, one folder for each snapshot, named with the UTC date and time, for example `20260924T020000Z`, and a link `latest` to the newest good snapshot.

Each snapshot folder holds:

- `tree`: all the files of the home;
- `backup.json`: a small record with the user, the time, the mode, the number of files and bytes, the excluded patterns, and the workspaces that were open.

A snapshot looks like a full copy. Files that did not change since the last snapshot are shared with it on disk (hard links). So many snapshots take little more space than one. Deleting one snapshot does not break another.

The snapshot folders are private to the owner of the files. They hold secrets. Treat the backup folder like the home itself.

You can open `tree` with any file manager and copy a single file out. You do not need the plugin to read a backup.

### The snapshot list

The dialog lists the snapshots of the home, newest first. Each row shows the time, the size, the number of files and the mode. Two labels can appear:

- **(pre-restore safety snapshot)**: made by a restore. See below.
- **(incomplete)**: the snapshot record says it did not finish. Do not restore it.

Each row has **Restore…** and **Delete…**. Both are dimmed while a backup or restore of the home runs.

> [!WARNING]
> **Delete…** removes one snapshot from the backup folder for good. You cannot restore it afterwards. The confirmation **Delete this snapshot?** names the time, size and files. It removes only that snapshot. The home and the other snapshots stay.

## Restore

A restore puts a snapshot back into the home. It always runs as a cold job. It closes every workspace of the user first, because it replaces the files that the agents use.

### Restore a snapshot

1. Press **Config backup…** on the card of the home.
2. In the list, find the snapshot and press **Restore…**. Expect: a dialog **Restore name’s home?**
3. Read the facts: the time, warm or cold, the number of files and the size. A warm snapshot shows a yellow line: it may not be perfectly consistent.
4. Choose **Replace** or **Merge** (see the table).
5. Keep the box **Take a safety snapshot of the current home first (labelled "pre-restore")** ticked, unless you have a good reason.
6. Press **Restore**. Expect: "Queued — Watch the activity tray for progress."

> [!WARNING]
> A restore closes every workspace of that user. In **Replace** mode, it also removes everything in the home that the snapshot does not hold. That includes work done after the snapshot was taken. The safety snapshot keeps that work. Do not untick it unless you are sure. One exception: a folder that the backup left out on purpose (the list in **Advanced: excluded files**, for example a cache folder) is not removed. The restore leaves it in the home as it is.

The plugin reopens the workspaces after the restore. A workspace that was working when it closed receives a Continue message. The dialog says so.

| Mode | Files only in the home | Files in both | Use it when |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Replace** (default) — "the home ends up identical to the snapshot; anything else in the home is removed" | Removed. | Taken from the snapshot. | The home is damaged, or you want the exact state of the snapshot. |
| **Merge** — "the snapshot's files are copied over the home; nothing else is removed" | Kept. | Taken from the snapshot. | You want to bring back some files and keep what you made since. |

In **Merge** mode, the snapshot's copy wins for every file that the snapshot holds. A newer file in the home with the same name is overwritten.

### The safety snapshot

Before it changes the home, the plugin makes one more snapshot of the home as it is. It is an ordinary cold snapshot in the same backup folder, labelled "pre-restore". It appears in the list.

If the restore was a mistake, restore the safety snapshot. This puts the home back as it was. Like any snapshot, the safety snapshot can be removed by **Keep** when many more backups run. Restore it soon if you need it.

If the plugin cannot make the safety snapshot, it does not go on with the restore. It reopens the workspaces.

### Progress and the "Last restore" line

While a restore runs, the dialog shows the step: pre-flight, closing, safety-snapshot, restoring, verifying, baking and relaunching. The Activity tray shows the same steps.

When it ends, the dialog shows a line under the snapshot list:

- **Last restore:** time, "from" the snapshot, the mode, and "— safety snapshot kept". The restore worked.
- **Last restore:** time, snapshot, mode, "— failed" and the cause, then "Safety snapshot kept at" a path. The restore failed.

If no restore has run, the line reads "No restore yet."

A failed restore does not undo itself. If it fails after the copy began, the home stays as the copy left it. Restore the safety snapshot to go back. The Health check also warns when the last restore failed.

### Checks before a restore

The plugin checks these things before it closes any workspace. If a check fails, it ends the job with one sentence and changes nothing:

- The snapshot folder exists, holds a record for the same user, and holds `tree`.
- The home is mounted and not halted.
- The home has room: at least the size of the snapshot for **Replace**, and 1.2 times that for **Merge**.
- For a safety snapshot, the backup folder passes the same checks as a backup.

### The command line

You can list and restore from a shell.

| Command | What it does |
| :-- | :-- |
| `php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/scripts/admin-agent.php list-backups root` | Lists the snapshots of the user `root`. It changes nothing. |
| `php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/scripts/admin-agent.php restore-home root --snapshot=latest` | Prints the plan and exits with code 2. It changes nothing. |
| `php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/scripts/admin-agent.php restore-home root --snapshot=latest --mode=merge --yes` | Restores at once, with no further question. |

For `--snapshot`, give a snapshot folder or the word `latest`. The default mode is `replace`. Add `--no-safety-snapshot` to skip the safety snapshot. Run these commands in your own shell: an SSH session or the Terminal button of Unraid.

> [!WARNING]
> `--yes` starts the restore at once. It closes every workspace of the user and, in replace mode, removes files. Run the command without `--yes` first and read the plan.

The command with `--yes` refuses to run inside an agent workspace. It checks for the marker that every workspace carries, in its own process and in the processes above it. The reason is simple: a restore closes every workspace of the user, including the agent that runs the command. An agent also must not change its own home without your approval.

An agent that wants a restore does it this way: it proposes the restore through the admin tool `aicli_restore_home`. The proposal appears in the Activity tray as a pending item. You approve it there, or you reject it. The agent cannot approve its own proposal. The same holds for a backup that an agent proposes with `aicli_backup_home`. The tool `aicli_list_backups` only reads the list. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md).

## Choices and settings

All of these are per home. They live in the **Backup** dialog and save at once.

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Destination folder** | The folder that holds the snapshots. | None | Always set it first. Use a drive other than the one with your layers. |
| **Mode** | **Cold** closes the workspaces. **Warm** does not. | **Cold** | Choose warm only when a pause is not acceptable. |
| **Keep** | How many snapshots to hold (1 to 50). | 5 | Raise it for more history. Lower it to save space. |
| **Schedule** | **Off**, **Daily** at a time, or **Weekly** on a day and time. | **Off** | Set a daily schedule for a home you use every day. |
| **Continue on relaunch** | Sends one Continue message to each agent that was working. | Ticked | Untick it to save tokens. |
| **Advanced: excluded files** | Patterns of files the copy skips. | A list of caches | Add large folders that you can recreate. |

## What happens behind the scenes

A backup is a job in the same queue as saves and merges. Only one storage job runs on a home at a time. The copy runs at a low priority, so it does not slow the server much. The plugin copies the files, then compares the copy with the home. Only a clean comparison counts as a good snapshot. A failed copy is deleted and `latest` still points to the last good snapshot. The plugin always reopens the workspaces, even when the backup fails. For the design, see C4 Component: Storage Management.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Config backup is not set up.** | No folder is chosen. | Press **Set up config backup…** and choose a folder. |
| **Last config backup failed:** a reason | The job stopped. The plugin removed the partial snapshot. | Read the reason. Common causes: the drive is gone, there is no room, or a file differed from the home. Fix the cause and press **Back up now**. |
| The result line shows a cross | The plugin refuses the folder. | Read the reason. Choose a folder on a pool, a disk or an Unassigned Devices drive. |
| **Not saved:** a reason | A value was refused. | The field shows the last saved value. Enter an allowed value. **Keep** must be from 1 to 50. |
| "Could not load the backup settings." | The dialog could not read the settings. | Press **Try again**. |
| "Snapshot list unavailable." | The plugin cannot read the backup folder. | Check that the drive is present. Reopen the dialog. |
| **Back up now** is dimmed | No folder is set, or a backup or restore of the home runs. | Hover over the button. It tells you which. |
| A message "Storage tidy-up in progress" | A merge runs on the home. | Wait a few minutes, then try again. |
| "N files changed during the backup" | A warm backup ran while agents worked. | Nothing. The snapshot is complete. |
| A snapshot is marked **(incomplete)** | It did not finish. | Delete it. Do not restore it. |
| Health warns about an old backup | No good snapshot within twice the schedule interval. | Run a backup. Check the schedule and the drive. |
| A restore is refused with one sentence | A check failed before anything closed. | Read the sentence. Typical causes: the home is halted, the drive is not mounted, or there is no room. |
| "The backup place … is on a network share, and the share is not mounted." | The folder is on a network share (for example under `/mnt/remotes`), and the share is not connected. A backup or restore would use an empty local folder. | Mount the share in Unassigned Devices, check that the server is on, then try again. The plugin changes no snapshot while the share is not mounted. |
| "The backup place … is mounted, but the plugin cannot write to it." | The share is connected, but it takes no writes. The share may be read-only, or the server may not answer. | Check that the share is online and not read-only. Then press **Back up now** again. |
| **Last restore** shows "— failed" | The restore stopped. The home stays as the copy left it. | Restore the safety snapshot named in the line. |
| `restore-home` says it refuses to run | You ran it inside an agent workspace. | Run it in your own shell. |
